title: Is there a friend for life
titleChinese: 是否存在一辈子的朋友？
paragraphs: Who do you count as your friends? From our BFF to a work mate, it’s good to have someone to chew the fat with or offer comfort and support. But when it comes to friendship, is it more important to have quantity or quality?

The recent isolation we have endured due to the coronavirus pandemic has made some of us question our friendships. We’ve fallen out of touch with friends and acquaintances, and it may feel awkward, but do we actually have to rekindle every relationship we once had? It might be time to take stock and think about who you kept in touch with, who you missed talking to, and who you didn’t. In short, maybe it’s time to reset your list of real mates.

There’s no obligation to stay friends, and writing for BBC Worklife, Bryan Lufkin says: “While people have known for years that friendships are unquestionably good for your health, experts say it’s only natural for acquaintances and even friends to fall by the wayside as time goes on – and it’s nothing to feel guilty about.”

Of course, it can be hard to choose who’s in your friendship circle. This is what Suzanne Degges-White, professor of counselling at Northern Illinois University, calls our ‘friendscape’. She says, “in life, as we go through certain stages and ages, our attention shifts, and we want to be around people who are like us.”

So, changing friends is normal, but we still need those special pals who’ve known us long term. These are friendships we invest time in. According to Robin Dunbar, a professor of evolutionary psychology at the University of Oxford, these are your inner circle of friends – your “shoulders to cry on” – and you have to see them at least once a week to keep them in that circle. He adds that the friends that do drift are mostly “friendships of convenience”. But the advice for maintaining a good friendship is to share how you feel with someone you trust – this can help strengthen your friendship as well as giving you both a chance to support each other.

vocabulary.entry: BFF /ˌbiː ef ˈef/ n. 最好的朋友（全称best friend forever）
vocabulary.example: She has been my BFF since we were in primary school.
vocabulary.translation: 她从小学起就是我最好的朋友。

vocabulary.entry: work mate /ˈwɜːk meɪt/ n. 同事；工友
vocabulary.example: My work mate helped me finish the difficult task on time.
vocabulary.translation: 我的同事帮我按时完成了这项艰巨的任务。

vocabulary.entry: chew the fat /tʃuː ðə fæt/ 闲聊；侃大山
vocabulary.example: We often chew the fat over a cup of coffee after work.
vocabulary.translation: 下班后我们经常喝着咖啡闲聊。

vocabulary.entry: quantity /ˈkwɒntəti/ n. 数量；数目
vocabulary.example: Quality is more important than quantity when it comes to choosing friends.
vocabulary.translation: 择友时，质量比数量更重要。

vocabulary.entry: quality /ˈkwɒləti/ n. 质量；品质
vocabulary.example: The watch is cheap, but its quality is surprisingly good.
vocabulary.translation: 这块手表价格便宜，但质量却出奇地好。

vocabulary.entry: isolation /ˌaɪsəˈleɪʃn/ n. 隔离；孤立
vocabulary.example: The long period of isolation made her appreciate social interactions more.
vocabulary.translation: 长时间的隔离让她更加珍惜社交互动。

vocabulary.entry: endure /ɪnˈdjʊə(r)/ v. 忍受；忍耐
vocabulary.example: She had to endure a lot of pain after the accident.
vocabulary.translation: 事故后她不得不忍受巨大的痛苦。

vocabulary.entry: fall out of touch with /fɔːl aʊt əv tʌtʃ wɪð/ 与……失去联系
vocabulary.example: I fell out of touch with my childhood friend after moving to another city.
vocabulary.translation: 搬到另一个城市后，我就和儿时的朋友失去了联系。

vocabulary.entry: acquaintance /əˈkweɪntəns/ n. 熟人；相识的人
vocabulary.example: He is just an acquaintance, not a close friend of mine.
vocabulary.translation: 他只是个熟人，不是我的密友。

vocabulary.entry: awkward /ˈɔːkwəd/ adj. 令人尴尬的；不自在的
vocabulary.example: It was awkward when we met each other after the argument.
vocabulary.translation: 争吵后我们碰面，场面很尴尬。

vocabulary.entry: rekindle /ˌriːˈkɪndl/ v. 重新点燃；恢复（关系）
vocabulary.example: They tried to rekindle their friendship after years of separation.
vocabulary.translation: 多年分离后，他们试图恢复往日的友谊。

vocabulary.entry: take stock /teɪk stɒk/ 评估；审视
vocabulary.example: It's time to take stock of your life and set new goals.
vocabulary.translation: 是时候审视你的人生并设定新目标了。

vocabulary.entry: reset /ˌriːˈset/ v. 重置；重新设定
vocabulary.example: She decided to reset her priorities and spend more time with family.
vocabulary.translation: 她决定重新设定自己的优先事项，花更多时间陪伴家人。

vocabulary.entry: mate /meɪt/ n. 朋友；伙伴
vocabulary.example: My old mate from college is coming to visit me this weekend.
vocabulary.translation: 我大学时的老朋友这周末要来看我。

vocabulary.entry: obligation /ˌɒblɪˈɡeɪʃn/ n. 义务；责任
vocabulary.example: You have no obligation to accept this invitation.
vocabulary.translation: 你没有义务接受这份邀请。

vocabulary.entry: unquestionably /ʌnˈkwestʃənəbli/ adv. 毫无疑问地；无可争议地
vocabulary.example: Her dedication to work is unquestionably admirable.
vocabulary.translation: 她对工作的投入无疑令人钦佩。

vocabulary.entry: fall by the wayside /fɔːl baɪ ðə ˈweɪsaɪd/ 被搁置；被抛弃；逐渐消失
vocabulary.example: Many good plans fall by the wayside due to lack of funding.
vocabulary.translation: 许多好计划因缺乏资金而被搁置。

vocabulary.entry: guilty /ˈɡɪlti/ adj. 内疚的；有罪的
vocabulary.example: She felt guilty for forgetting her best friend's birthday.
vocabulary.translation: 她因为忘记了闺蜜的生日而感到内疚。

vocabulary.entry: friendship circle /ˈfrendʃɪp ˈsɜːkl/ 朋友圈子
vocabulary.example: She likes to expand her friendship circle by joining different clubs.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢通过参加不同的俱乐部来扩大自己的朋友圈子。

vocabulary.entry: counselling /ˈkaʊnsəlɪŋ/ n. 咨询；辅导
vocabulary.example: The university offers free counselling services to all students.
vocabulary.translation: 这所大学为所有学生提供免费的咨询服务。

vocabulary.entry: friendscape /ˈfrendskeɪp/ n. 人际圈；交友版图
vocabulary.example: As we grow older, our friendscape tends to become smaller but more stable.
vocabulary.translation: 随着年龄增长，我们的交友版图往往会变小但更稳定。

vocabulary.entry: shift /ʃɪft/ v. 转变；转移
vocabulary.example: Public opinion has shifted in favour of the new policy.
vocabulary.translation: 公众舆论已转向支持这项新政策。

vocabulary.entry: pal /pæl/ n. 朋友；老兄
vocabulary.example: Hey pal, long time no see! How have you been?
vocabulary.translation: 嘿，老兄，好久不见！你过得怎么样？

vocabulary.entry: invest /ɪnˈvest/ v. 投入（时间、精力等）
vocabulary.example: It's important to invest time and effort in maintaining good friendships.
vocabulary.translation: 投入时间和精力维护良好的友谊很重要。

vocabulary.entry: evolutionary psychology /ˌiːvəˈluːʃənri saɪˈkɒlədʒi/ 进化心理学
vocabulary.example: Evolutionary psychology studies how human behaviour has evolved over time.
vocabulary.translation: 进化心理学研究人类行为是如何随时间演变的。

vocabulary.entry: inner circle /ˈɪnə ˈsɜːkl/ 核心圈子；亲信
vocabulary.example: Only a few people are in the manager's inner circle.
vocabulary.translation: 只有少数几个人在经理的核心圈子里。

vocabulary.entry: shoulders to cry on /ˈʃəʊldəz tu kraɪ ɒn/ 可以倾诉的对象；靠山
vocabulary.example: Whenever I feel upset, my sister is always my shoulders to cry on.
vocabulary.translation: 每当我心情不好时，姐姐永远是我可以倾诉的对象。

vocabulary.entry: drift /drɪft/ v. 逐渐疏远
vocabulary.example: They used to be close friends, but they drifted apart after graduation.
vocabulary.translation: 他们曾经是亲密的朋友，但毕业后就渐渐疏远了。

vocabulary.entry: friendships of convenience /ˈfrendʃɪps əv kənˈviːniəns/ 功利性友谊；因便利而建立的友谊
vocabulary.example: Friendships of convenience usually don't last long.
vocabulary.translation: 功利性友谊通常不会长久。

vocabulary.entry: maintain /meɪnˈteɪn/ v. 维持；保持
vocabulary.example: Regular communication is key to maintaining a healthy friendship.
vocabulary.translation: 定期沟通是维持健康友谊的关键。

sentences.english: Who do you count as your friends?
sentences.chinese: 你把谁看作自己的朋友？

sentences.english: From our BFF to a work mate, it’s good to have someone to chew the fat with or offer comfort and support.
sentences.chinese: 从最好的挚友到职场同事，身边能有个人聊聊天、给予安慰和支持，总归是件好事。

sentences.english: But when it comes to friendship, is it more important to have quantity or quality?
sentences.chinese: 但说到友谊，到底是数量重要，还是质量更重要呢？

sentences.english: The recent isolation we have endured due to the coronavirus pandemic has made some of us question our friendships.
sentences.chinese: 新冠疫情让我们经历了一段与世隔绝的时光，这也让有些人开始重新审视自己的友谊。

sentences.english: We’ve fallen out of touch with friends and acquaintances, and it may feel awkward, but do we actually have to rekindle every relationship we once had?
sentences.chinese: 我们与一些朋友和熟人渐渐失去了联系，或许再联系时会感到尴尬，但我们真的有必要重拾每一段过去的关系吗？

sentences.english: It might be time to take stock and think about who you kept in touch with, who you missed talking to, and who you didn’t.
sentences.chinese: 或许是时候好好审视一番，想想疫情期间你一直保持联系的人是谁，想念的聊天对象是谁，而那些你完全不想联系的又是谁。

sentences.english: In short, maybe it’s time to reset your list of real mates.
sentences.chinese: 简而言之，或许是时候重新整理你真正的朋友清单了。

sentences.english: There’s no obligation to stay friends, and writing for BBC Worklife, Bryan Lufkin says: “While people have known for years that friendships are unquestionably good for your health, experts say it’s only natural for acquaintances and even friends to fall by the wayside as time goes on – and it’s nothing to feel guilty about.”
sentences.chinese: 维持友谊并非一种义务，布莱恩·勒夫金在为BBC职场生活频道撰稿时表示：“尽管人们很早就知道，友谊对健康的益处毋庸置疑，但专家称，随着时间流逝，一些熟人甚至朋友逐渐疏远是很自然的事——对此完全不必感到羞愧。”

sentences.english: Of course, it can be hard to choose who’s in your friendship circle.
sentences.chinese: 当然，筛选自己的朋友圈并非易事。

sentences.english: This is what Suzanne Degges-White, professor of counselling at Northern Illinois University, calls our ‘friendscape’.
sentences.chinese: 北伊利诺伊大学的心理咨询学教授苏珊娜·德格斯-怀特将其称为我们的“人际圈”。

sentences.english: She says, “in life, as we go through certain stages and ages, our attention shifts, and we want to be around people who are like us.”
sentences.chinese: 她表示：“人生路上，随着我们经历不同的阶段、年岁渐长，注意力会发生转移，我们会更愿意和与自己志同道合的人相处。”

sentences.english: So, changing friends is normal, but we still need those special pals who’ve known us long term.
sentences.chinese: 所以，朋友的更迭是很正常的事，但我们依然需要那些相识多年的挚友。

sentences.english: These are friendships we invest time in.
sentences.chinese: 这类友谊是我们倾注了时间去经营的。

sentences.english: According to Robin Dunbar, a professor of evolutionary psychology at the University of Oxford, these are your inner circle of friends – your “shoulders to cry on” – and you have to see them at least once a week to keep them in that circle.
sentences.chinese: 牛津大学进化心理学教授罗宾·邓巴表示，这些人是你核心朋友圈里的人——是你“值得倾诉的对象”，想要维系这份情谊，你至少每周要和他们见一次面。

sentences.english: He adds that the friends that do drift are mostly “friendships of convenience”.
sentences.chinese: 他还补充道，那些渐渐疏远的朋友，大多只是“利益之交”。

sentences.english: But the advice for maintaining a good friendship is to share how you feel with someone you trust – this can help strengthen your friendship as well as giving you both a chance to support each other.
sentences.chinese: 而维系一段真挚友谊的秘诀，就是向你信任的人倾诉心声——这不仅能巩固你们的友谊，也能让彼此都有机会互相扶持。
